target_customer: Mid and large companies with corporate travel programs
problem: Employees spend company travel money carelessly because they gain nothing from saving; Rocketrip sets budgets and shares savings with employees as rewards.
business_model: B2B SaaS tied to travel savings, integrated with Concur, Sabre GetThere and Expensify

founders.name: Dan Ruch
founders.background_notes: YC blog says he and Gillian Tee were inspired by Googlers being rewarded for saving on travel. Prior employers not verified from an opened source.

founders.name: Gillian Tee
founders.background_notes: Named as founder in a YC blog post found in search results; not opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed price prediction algorithms (described as patented) plus integrations with corporate booking and expense tools.

defensibility.rationale: Patented budgeting algorithms and integrations with Concur and Sabre created some stickiness, but travel platforms could add similar rewards.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Concur became a partner rather than copying it; Mondee bought the company in September 2020, which Skift framed as a safe landing during the pandemic.

market_need_then: Companies were under pressure on travel costs; Rocketrip's customers by 2020 included iHeartMedia, Feld Entertainment and Twitter per Skift. Founding idea came from Google's practice of rewarding employee savings.

branding.domain_note: Used rocketrip.com, an exact .com; it now redirects to tabhi.com and then tabhi.ai.

brand_strength.rationale: No sources describe logo, mascot or community; the name conveys travel and rewards clearly but is confusable with Rocket-named travel brands like Rocketmiles.

outcome_analysis: Rocketrip raised about 14.6 million across 2014 to 2018 rounds I could source, grew to a team of 68, and sold to Mondee in September 2020 at an undisclosed price. Skift described the sale as a safe landing amid the pandemic travel collapse, so it was likely not a strong exit, though the price is unknown.
notes: YC page lists no founders. Founder names come from YC blog link and Skift speaker bio in search results, not opened, so prior employers and education are null. The July 2014 round was called an A1 extension, so stage is other. The April 2018 round amount comes from an AlleyWatch headline; a search summary called it Series C but the headline does not, so stage is other. Total funding estimates conflict: Skift 17.1M by 2016, CB Insights 31.15M, Preqin 15M, ZoomInfo 29.8M. No dated 2014 competitor found; later competitor lists are modern. Website fetch redirects to a different domain, tabhi.com, which I did not confirm as related.
